prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Asset: the first of two coordinated normal adult breast anatomy illustrations for a curious-reader teaching page.
Primary request: show the physical branching geometry of ONE illustrative terminal duct lobular unit (TDLU), not a flowchart. A hollow terminal duct connects a group of hollow glandular acini to a larger duct. Show how stroma lies around AND BETWEEN the individual structures.
Composition: square, one generous tactile tissue cutaway, with a short question heading and very large legible sans-serif labels. Detailed warm hand-drawn educational cartoon, softly textured watercolor/gouache, rounded scientific objects and subtle depth. No decorative people, faces or emojis. Soft rose luminal cells, muted sage nucleated myoepithelial cells, a thin blue extracellular basement membrane line, warm sand connective stroma. These are drawing conventions, not real tissue colors. Keep this palette and cell vocabulary for the second illustration.
Scene: a larger hollow duct enters from the left and connects to ONE smaller terminal duct branching into a loose cluster of several small acini. The acini are visibly hollow glandular sacs, not solid grapes. Selected cutaways reveal continuous connected lumina through the branches. Do not show any pathway arrow or milk motion. Put a bracket spanning the terminal duct and its associated acini, excluding the larger duct; label that grouping TDLU. The bracket is only an annotation, never a biological capsule. Acini are separated by connective stroma; do not surround the whole cluster with a shared basement-membrane envelope. Each duct/acinus has its own inner rose epithelial cells, outer sage living myoepithelial cells with nuclei, and a thin acellular blue basement membrane immediately outside those cells. Their fine layers are supporting detail here; the second illustration will magnify them. Stroma contains modest connective fibers and a spindle-shaped fibroblast outside the epithelial walls.
Text, verbatim and no other words: heading "What belongs to one TDLU?"; labels "Larger duct", "Terminal duct", "Acini", "TDLU", "Stroma"; small bottom note "Normal schematic • counts vary". Label Acini points to an individual hollow sac, Terminal duct points to its hollow branch, Stroma points to the space BETWEEN sacs. TDLU labels the grouping bracket, not one cell. Use pointer lines without directional arrowheads; all endpoints hit the named object. Large labels, strong contrast, ample whitespace; no mini text cards.
Accuracy: one illustrative NORMAL adult unit, not a universal lobe/acinus count and not cancer-cell ancestry. The relationships are anatomical nesting/connectivity, not progression, invasion or metastasis. No tumors, malignant cells, diagnostic specimen identifiers, RNA readout, stains, scale bar or numeric proportions. Cell plasma membranes and extracellular basement membrane are different. Do not draw myoepithelial cells as an acellular matrix stripe.

LIGHT THEME RENDERING ONLY: warm pale ivory background, quiet soft pastel fills and dark readable ink. Keep the scientific geometry and exact labels specified above. Produce one native square PNG.
